items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I don't know if you ever heard of John Moreira. Sure. John Moreira to me was the greatest banjo player I've ever heard in my life.

ctx.x: It seemed to me it was very good, but I wouldn't swear to him.

Well, Caffrey Dallas, boy, was one of the greatest I ever heard. And he used to play up here with Manuel in the band at the old roof corner. With Manuel Borreiro. Right. And he left here and he went to Dallas. He sent him to Dallas and of course he sent for his brother later on Percy. Percy and I were good friends, but so was Caffrey and I. Caffrey was a genius. He was just like John Moreira. I don't know if you ever heard of John Moreira. Sure. John Moreira to me was the greatest banjo player I've ever heard in…

So it may well have been him on that date. Yeah, I'm sure it does. I'm almost positive. You don't remember him being in the studio or anything? Yes, I do. You remember him being there? Yes, I do. Oh, well that's great. I'm glad to know.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: And John Moreira was the other [great banjo player].

ctx.x: He's a fine fellow. Oh yeah, I know Joe. I talked with him when I was in Washington. I did too.

There's another Dyeronsburg who played violin in New Orleans. Yes, that's another old one. But they don't tie in together with this Caffrey. Caffrey had a brother Percy, but both of them died in Dallas. But Caffrey Dyeronsburg, I often hear guys talk about great banjo players. There were only two. And Caffrey was one of them. And John Moreira was the other. Yeah.
